name: The Neural Bricklayers — weekly episode (front-end for the YakYak engine)

parameters.content:
## 📄 YakYak Description — workflow summary (not a step note)
Every Wednesday at UTC 06:00 the past week's X/Twitter posts from five AI titans (Sam Altman, Yann LeCun, Geoffrey Hinton, Andrej Karpathy, Elon Musk) are fetched, clustered into the single most controversial theme, and turned into a LEGO panel-debate episode moderated by Bob Brikko.

nodes.name: Show config
nodes.notes: ALL per-show config lives here, on the canvas — the workflow reads no environment variables. Required: campaignId (a campaign the API credential's account owns) and userId (for the balance check). Optional: soundtrackAudioPath (prefilled with the BBN intro track's content address — the beta/ prefix is normal, see docs/forking.md; empty = skip the pin), chatWebhookUrl (empty = no announcement). postToSocial=true is POST="true" parity — every run publishes to the campaign's linked networks (irreversible); set false for review-first runs.

nodes.name: Fetch user
nodes.notes: Same 'YakYak API' Bearer credential as the engine — no token on the canvas or in env. onError=continue so Balance guard can report a clear error instead of a bare 404.

parameters.jsCode:
// The Neural Bricklayers head-writer prompt, adapted from the BBN pattern
// (docs/the_neural_bricklayers.md in the yakyak repo). Sources are X/Twitter
// timelines via nitter RSS (+ Google News for Hinton, who barely posts).
// Per-account lookbacks (Musk 3d, others 5d, Hinton 14d) are enforced by the
// prompt against each item's <pubDate>. One overarching theme per episode;
// 12 scenes; fixed studio; fixed outfits; co-panelists visible in every shot.
const trim = (s) => String(s || '').slice(0, 15000);
const src = (label, s) => s ? `--- ${label} ---\n${s}` : `--- ${label} ---\n(source unavailable this run — proceed without it)`;
const musk = trim(($('Fetch Musk (X)').first().json || {}).data);
const altman = trim(($('Fetch Altman (X)').first().json || {}).data);
const lecun = trim(($('Fetch LeCun (X)').first().json || {}).data);
const karpathy = trim(($('Fetch Karpathy (X)').first().json || {}).data);
const hinton = trim(($('Fetch Hinton (news)').first().json || {}).data);
const got = [musk, altman, lecun, karpathy, hinton].filter(Boolean).length;
if (got < 2) throw new Error(`only ${got}/5 sources fetched — not enough material for a debate (nitter may be rate-limiting; retry later)`);
const ts = new Date().toISOString();

const prompt = `You are the head writer for "The Neural Bricklayers", a satirical
short-form panel-debate show: the five most influential voices in AI, rendered as
LEGO-style plastic minifigure caricatures, argue on a late-night TV set. The
debates are PARODY, but every episode is seeded from things the panelists
really posted this week. Your job in this run is to produce ONE episode.

STEP 1 — Read the source material below (RSS mirrors of each panelist's real
X/Twitter timeline, plus a news feed for Hinton). Each <item> has a <pubDate>.
Apply these lookback windows from now (now: ${ts}):
  - Elon Musk: past 3 days only (he posts constantly; older items are stale).
  - Sam Altman, Yann LeCun, Andrej Karpathy: past 5 days.
  - Geoffrey Hinton (news feed): past 14 days.
Ignore items outside the window. Retweets ("RT by @…") count as endorsements —
usable, but prefer the panelist's own words. If a source is marked unavailable,
note it and give that panelist positions consistent with their well-known views.

STEP 2 — Find THE CLASH. Cluster the posts by topic and pick the ONE theme with
the most heat — the sharpest real disagreement between at least three panelists.
That single theme is the episode's spine: every scene must advance it. Pick the
most exciting, most controversial defensible reading of what they posted; real
friction between the actual posts beats invented drama.

STEP 3 — Write the episode.

THE STUDIO (identical in every scene — restate it, do not vary it):
The Neural Bricklayers studio — a late-night debate set built entirely from toy
plastic bricks: one long curved glossy black brick desk, six brick microphones,
purple-and-teal rim lighting, a glowing brick LED backdrop reading "THE NEURAL
BRICKLAYERS", and a brick city-skyline window behind the desk. Fixed seating,
left to right: Sam Altman, Yann LeCun, Bob Brikko (center, moderator), Geoffrey
Hinton, Andrej Karpathy, Elon Musk. Same studio, same seats, all 12 scenes.

CAST — fixed outfits (repeat the outfit EVERY time a character appears; never
change or omit it):
  - Bob Brikko (moderator) — rumpled tan trench coat over a white shirt, crooked
    press badge. Tongue-in-cheek, dry, deadpan under fire.
  - Sam Altman — plain gray crewneck sweater under an open dark-blue jacket.
    The Operator: smooth, always announcing, deflects doom with scale.
  - Yann LeCun — brown tweed blazer, light-blue shirt, thick black rectangular
    glasses. The Contrarian Scientist: unimpressed, fights billionaires for sport.
  - Geoffrey Hinton — charcoal suit, slate-gray shirt, autumn-leaf patterned tie,
    white hair. The Conscience: gentle, wry, quietly terrifying.
  - Andrej Karpathy — plain dark-charcoal t-shirt, silver laptop under one arm.
    The Builder: earnest, permanently amazed, the only one who still writes code.
  - Elon Musk — black tuxedo-style jacket over an open-collar white shirt,
    tousled hair, smirk. The Accelerant: announces, provokes and memes in one breath.

EPISODE STRUCTURE — exactly 12 scenes. Bob opens and closes; every panelist
leads EXACTLY TWO scenes:
  - Scene 1 — Bob Brikko: cold open, names the week's clash.
  - Scenes 2–6 — first round: each panelist's opening take (one scene each, any
    order that serves the drama).
  - Scenes 7–11 — second round: rebuttals and escalation — pair natural enemies
    back-to-back and let them answer each other (one scene each, any order).
  - Scene 12 — Bob Brikko: deadpan sign-off that lands the theme.

PER-SCENE REQUIREMENTS:
  - Roughly 200 words of prose describing the scene's visuals, action and
    atmosphere, written as a director briefing a camera op. EVERY scene's prose
    must: (a) open by re-establishing the same studio described above, (b) put
    the leading character front and center at their fixed seat with their exact
    fixed outfit, and (c) show AT LEAST TWO other named cast members visibly
    reacting in the frame (soft focus, at their own fixed seats, in their own
    fixed outfits — name them and describe their reaction).
  - Exactly ONE spoken dialog line per scene, 8–12 words, attributed to the
    scene's leading character. Do NOT end the dialog line with a period
    ("!" or "?" are fine).
  - Leading character must be from the cast. No other characters speak.

TONE: Satirical panel-show comedy with real bite. The heat comes from the
panelists' REAL public positions pushed to their logical extreme; exaggerate
delivery, not facts. No slapstick, no slurs, no fabricated scandals. Punch up,
not down.

STEP 4 — Reply with ONLY the markdown document below — no preamble, no
triple-backtick fences, nothing after it:

  # The Neural Bricklayers — Latest Debate
  **Generated (UTC):** ${ts}
  **Sources:** X/Twitter timelines (@elonmusk 3d, @sama/@ylecun/@karpathy 5d), Hinton news (14d)

  ## Social title: <punchy controversial title for social posting, 50 characters MAX>

  ## Theme: <one sentence naming the episode's single overarching clash>

  ## Posts we drew from:
  - <one bullet per real post/report you used: who, what, when>

  ## Scene 1 — <short title>
  **Leading character:** Bob Brikko
  **Dialog:** "<8–12 word line>"

  <~200 words of scene prose>

  ... (continue through Scene 12, which is again Bob Brikko) ...

===== SOURCE MATERIAL =====

${src('@elonmusk (nitter RSS)', musk)}

${src('@sama (nitter RSS)', altman)}

${src('@ylecun (nitter RSS)', lecun)}

${src('@karpathy (nitter RSS)', karpathy)}

${src('Geoffrey Hinton (Google News RSS)', hinton)}`;

return [{ json: { prompt } }];

nodes.name: Write story (Claude)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'claude-opus-4-8', max_tokens: 16000, thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, messages: [ { role: 'user', content: $json.prompt } ] } }}

nodes.notes: Messages API over raw HTTP (no SDK inside n8n). Auth via the 'Anthropic API key' Header Auth credential (header name x-api-key). Adaptive thinking; the story lands in the response's text block.

nodes.name: Build story payload
nodes.notes: The story markdown is preserved on this node's output — n8n's execution log is the story archive (the showrunner's stories/ equivalent).

nodes.name: Call engine

workflowId.cachedResultName: YakYak engine — resolve target, patch or new episode, render, post

nodes.notes: Fires the generic YakYak engine in episode mode. Timeout 45 min — the engine only responds once the episode is generated AND rendered. Retry is safe: a re-run lands on the same unrendered slot. Announcement happens here (below), not in the engine.

nodes.name: Set social fields

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ Object.assign({ movieId: $json.movieId }, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle ? { socialTitle: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle } : {}, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption ? { socialDescription: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption } : {}) }}

nodes.notes: Showrunner parity: ≤50-char social title (from the story call) + headline-derived caption. onError=continue — cosmetic metadata must not kill a rendered episode.

nodes.name: Announce

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { text: '🧱 The Neural Bricklayers episode ready — "' + ($('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle || 'Latest Debate') + '": ' + $('Call engine').item.json.url } }}

nodes.notes: Chat notification with the episode link. chatWebhookUrl empty → this node errors and the run still succeeds (onError=continue). Social posting happens in the three nodes after this one, gated by Show config postToSocial — see integrations/n8n/docs/breaking_bricks_news.md §4.3.

nodes.name: Fetch campaign links
nodes.notes: The campaign's linked social networks — GET /social/campaign-links, same call the showrunner makes before posting. Read-only, so it runs regardless; the postToSocial gate is applied in Build post list. onError=continue so Build post list can report a clear error.

nodes.name: Build post list
nodes.notes: One item per linked network. Linking networks to the campaign is a one-time manual step (yakyak.ai profile, or course/08-social-post) — with none linked, this emits zero items and the run still succeeds.

nodes.name: Post to socials
nodes.notes: POST /social/post-movie/{movieId}/{connectedNetworkId}, empty body — runs once per item, i.e. once per linked network. IRREVERSIBLE. onError=continue mirrors the showrunner: a per-network 4xx (mis-configured account etc.) must not fail the other networks or the run. Needs the social_publishing scope on the PAT.

nodes.name: Every Wednesday
nodes.notes: 06:00 UTC daily — CADENCE=daily in show/BreakingBricksNews/show.env. Use 'Test workflow' to fire a run by hand.
